title: Prime-power binomial coefficient divisibility
statement: Let $p$ be a prime natural number, $a\geq0$ a natural number, and $k$ a natural number with $0<k\leq p^a$. For a positive integer $t$, write $v_p(t)$ for the largest natural number $e$ such that $p^e$ divides $t$. Then $p^{a-v_p(k)}$ divides $\binom{p^a}{k}$ in $\mathbf N$, where subtraction in the exponent is truncated natural-number subtraction. Here $\binom Nk=N!/(k!(N-k)!)$ for $0\leq k\leq N$. Divisibility is ordinary integer divisibility in the commutative ring $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]: $u\mid v$ means $v=uc$ for an integer $c$; for $u>0$ and $v\geq0$ this is equivalent to divisibility in $\mathbf N$.
